one_liner: Arm's C library of DSP kernels for Cortex-M and Cortex-A; its FFTs beat textbook plain-C radix-2 FFTs on Cortex-M4.
what_it_does: A library of tuned compute kernels for Arm cores: basic and fast math, FIR/biquad filtering, transforms (complex and real FFT, DCT, MFCC), matrix ops, statistics and classical ML, in f64, f32, f16, q31, q15 and q7. The C API is instance-based: you pass a constant table struct (arm_cfft_sR_f32_len64) or call a length-specific init, then arm_cfft_f32(S, buf, ifftFlag, bitReverseFlag) transforms interleaved complex data in place. It is not a drop-in for a textbook FFT routine: the signature, scaling and init step differ. An optional header-only C++ layer (DSP++) adds loop fusion, and a pip package (cmsisdsp) mirrors the C API in Python.
how_it_is_fast: The f32 complex FFT is a mixed-radix decimation-in-frequency transform: several radix-8 stages plus one radix-2 or radix-4 stage, driven by precomputed per-length twiddle and bit-reversal tables, so no trig or twiddle recurrence runs at transform time. Q15/Q31 FFTs use radix-4 stages plus one radix-2 stage with a fixed down-scale in each stage to avoid overflow. Separate code paths use Helium (MVE) vector butterflies with rearranged twiddle tables on Cortex-M55/M85 and Ne10-derived mixed-radix kernels on Neon; fixed-point kernels read a 32-bit word as two q15 or four q7 values. Part of the large float gap in the cited benchmark is probably the baseline: the Numerical Recipes routine keeps its twiddle recurrence in double, which a single-precision Cortex-M4F FPU must emulate (inference, not measured).
when_to_use: Firmware on Cortex-M4/M7/M33 (DSP extension, single-precision FPU) or Cortex-M55/M85 (Helium) that needs power-of-two FFTs of 16 to 4096 points, FIR or biquad filters, or small matrix kernels.
Fixed-point (q15/q31) signal chains on cores without an FPU, where the library's fixed per-stage scaling is acceptable.
Projects already on CMSIS packs, Keil/Arm Compiler 6 or Zephyr: it ships as a CMSIS pack and as a Zephyr module, so integration is a west or pack entry.
Designing a signal chain in Python with the cmsisdsp wrapper (NumPy-compatible, fixed-point aware) and porting the same calls to C.
Arm application processors (aarch64 with Neon) when you want one DSP API across MCU and Cortex-A targets, accepting the different Neon FFT API.
when_not_to_use: x86 or other non-Arm production targets: host builds compile as portable scalar C with none of the Arm-specific vector paths.
FFT sizes that are not powers of two between 16 and 4096 (the documented arm_cfft range), or when you need mixed radix-3/5 lengths.
Work that needs bit-identical output across cores: the docs say some algorithms give slightly different results on M0, M4/M7 and M55 as a speed trade-off.
Fixed-point FFTs that need full dynamic range: Q31 input is 1.31 but output is shifted down (5.27 at 16 points up to 11.21 at 1024), so low-order bits are lost.

Toolchains you cannot tune: the README says GCC currently gives poor Helium code (use the Arm compiler) and that -fno-builtin has a very bad impact; the older radix-2/radix-4 functions are deprecated and slower, and a plain-C fixed-point FFT (SYLT-FFT) reported 15-26% faster than the deprecated arm_cfft_radix2_q31 from CMSIS-DSP 1.4.2 at 256 points.

integration.form: static lib or source-drop (build Source, Include, PrivateInclude; also a CMSIS pack, a Zephyr module and a CMake package exporting CMSISDSP::CMSISDSP); the DSP++ C++ layer is header-only
integration.dependencies: CMSIS-Core headers for Cortex-M builds (HOST=ON removes this for host builds); the in-repo ComputeLibrary and Ne10 sources for Neon builds; nothing else
integration.min_toolchain: C11 in the repo's own build configs (-std=c11; DSP++ configs use -std=c++17); arm_math_types.h supports Arm Compiler 6, GCC, Clang, IAR, TI, Cosmic, Tasking and MSVC; CMake 3.14+ for the CMake build
integration.platforms: Cortex-M (scalar, DSP extension, Helium/MVE on M55/M85), Cortex-A and aarch64 with Neon (-DARM_MATH_NEON or cmake NEON=ON), plus scalar host builds on x86 Linux, Windows and macOS
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The docs say the FFT instance tables are constant and not modified during a transform, and transforms work on the caller's buffer, so concurrent transforms on separate buffers that share one instance should be safe (inference).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same in-place transform on interleaved complex data, but with a different call signature, a required instance or init call, different scaling (the inverse includes 1/N; Q31 output is down-shifted), and on Neon an out-of-place API with a temporary buffer

gotchas: arm_cfft_f32 runs in place and arm_rfft_fast_f32 overwrites its input; in issue #228 the maintainer says the only way to keep the input is a temporary copy.

Use length-specific init functions (arm_cfft_init_64_f32 and similar): the generic arm_cfft_init_f32 stops the linker from dropping unused twiddle tables, and the Helium build requires an init call rather than the constant structs.

Build flags decide the speed: the README asks for -O3 -ffast-math and an FPU-enabled target (else soft-float emulation); -fno-builtin stops the memcpy-based type punning from being inlined; some compilers need -munaligned-access; define DISABLEFLOAT16 if f16 is unused, since it can break compilation.

Neon builds change the f32 CFFT/RFFT API (separate input, output and temporary buffers, no bit-reverse flag), and DSP++ does not compile with ARM_MATH_NEON. Issue #247 (a Zephyr toolchain hitting an alignment fault in arm_rfft_init_q31 on Helium) was closed wontfix as a compiler problem.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick CMSIS-DSP for transforms, filters and fixed-point DSP on Arm microcontrollers. libfixmath covers scalar fixed-point arithmetic, and SLEEF, xsimd, SIMDe and NumKong target elementwise or vector math on application-class CPUs, so none of the catalogued siblings offers its FFT and filter kernels.
verified_claims_summary: An Arm Community post by an Arm intern (2013 per the verifier) timed CMSIS-DSP's float32 and Q31 complex FFTs against the Numerical Recipes radix-2 float FFT and a 32-bit adaptation of the Roberts/Slaney/Bouras fixed-point FFT on an STM32F407 (Cortex-M4F) at 30 MHz with zero flash wait states, built with Keil MDK 4.70a (flags not stated). The figures (about 35x faster for float with the FPU on, about 4x with it off, about 1.9x for Q31) come only from a search-result summary: the post was unreachable, two searches this session confirmed the setup but not the numbers, and the CMSIS-DSP version and FFT function used are not shown.
status_note: Actively maintained by Arm (last commit 2026-09-10; the CMake version fallback is 1.18.0), Apache-2.0, and distributed as a CMSIS pack, a Zephyr module and a pip wrapper, so it is easy to vendor.
